title: Razorpay Brings Payments to Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp Business app
summary: Razorpay brings payments to Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp, enabling Indian businesses to turn conversations into purchases with UPI, cards and netbanking.
body_markdown:
For a large share of India’s small businesses, WhatsApp is the primary sales channel. Customers discover products there, ask questions, compare options and decide what to buy. What has been missing is a reliable way to carry that intent through to payment without breaking the conversation.


We’re excited to announce that[Razorpay](https://razorpay.com/) is now live on Meta Business Agent on WhatsApp, in India. When a customer is ready to buy, the agent generates a Razorpay-powered payment link directly in the chat, and the customer pays using a method of their choice: UPI, cards or netbanking without leaving WhatsApp.


In a world moving quickly towards conversational commerce, this launch addresses a specific and well-understood gap in emerging conversational AI experiences: payments. With Razorpay and Meta’s partnership, this launch reflects a broader shift in how Indian consumers will come to discover and buy, and what that means for the businesses serving them.


## **Where conversational sales are lost today**


Messaging has become the default way customers want to engage with businesses.


*A Kantar study commissioned by Meta found that 75% of online adults want to communicate with businesses the way they do with friends and family: through messaging.*


For an SMB, however, handling that volume manually creates three recurring points of revenue leakage:


- **Response latency:** Enquiries that arrive after business hours, or while the owner is attending to orders or walk-in customers, often go unanswered long enough for the customer to move on. The effect is sharpest during festive periods, when enquiry volumes rise and owner bandwidth is at its lowest.


- **Repetitive handling cost:** Questions on price, availability, variants and delivery recur across conversations. Answering them consumes time that would otherwise go to operations and growth.


- **Payment friction:** A customer who has decided to buy can still drop off if payment requires switching apps, sharing details manually or waiting for the merchant to confirm.


Each of these affects the same metric: the share of conversations that end in a paid order. For a small business, this challenge is felt even more acutely.


## **What changes with this launch for business owners**


Meta Business Agent is an AI agent for WhatsApp Business that answers customer questions, recommends products and keeps conversations moving, in the customer’s own language. It operates within the WhatsApp inbox and WhatsApp Business app that merchants already use, and businesses can get started with 0 coding.


With this launch, Razorpay becomes the payments layer that augments the overall customers experience, by translating intent into purchases. The agent can now move a customer from enquiry to a successful payment within the conversation.


### **The flow**


1. A customer starts a conversation from an ad, a post, a catalogue or a direct message.


2. The agent responds, answers questions and recommends products based on the information the business has provided.


3. When the customer decides to buy, the agent generates a payment link powered by Razorpay.


4. The customer pays using their preferred method (UPI, cards or netbanking) in the same chat.


The customer completes discovery, decision and payment in one thread, and the merchant does not need to build or maintain a separate checkout journey for it.


## **Impact for small businesses**


Shoppers can ask questions, explore products and get assistance in their own language, whether they are looking for a gift hamper or checking whether a festive outfit is in stock, even when the owner is busy.


Once they have chosen, they pay through the[Razorpay-powered link](https://razorpay.com/payment-links/) in the same conversation. The experience is faster for the customer and more likely to end in a completed purchase for the business. This matters because personalised, responsive service is increasingly what customers expect.


*A Deloitte Digital research found that 80% of consumers prefer brands that offer personalised experiences, and that brands which delivered them saw 50% more spend* .


- **Continuous responsiveness:** The agent handles customer queries while owners focus on orders, inventory and in-store customers. Enquiries are answered at the moment they arrive, including outside business hours.


- **A shorter path from intent to payment:** Customers pay in the conversation where they made the decision. Removing the hand-off between enquiry and payment reduces the points at which a sale can be lost.


- **Operational capacity without added headcount:** Routine questions are automated, which frees owners and small teams to concentrate on higher-value conversations and on running the business.


- **Owner control by design:** Merchants decide when the agent is active, can step into any conversation at any point, and can route specific queries to a person. Automation covers the routine; judgement stays with the owner.


## **Why this matters**


As AI assistants become a new channel for discovering and shopping, payments must be part of the same experience rather than an afterthought. Razorpay has been investing in this shift through its work on agentic commerce. This launch extends that work to WhatsApp, where Indian businesses already engage their customers every day.


## **Getting started**


Meta Business Agent with Razorpay payments is available to eligible small businesses in India. If you’re a business owner who uses Razorpay as your payment gateway and sells on Meta, you can get started with


[Meta Business Agent](https://whatsappbusiness.com/products/business-app-ai-agent/) .


If you have any other questions, or need assistance, drop us a note here.
